geometry_edits.rationale: Replace the single cantilever block with a split-wing mass so the ground can open toward the access edge.
Split along the long axis to create a clearer central public void and street-facing threshold.
Open a substantial gap between masses to strengthen public void legibility.
Keep a ground-level connector so the two wings still read as one coherent building rather than fragments.
Make the new split-wing mass the root so the edited geometry re-centers around the public void and active ground threshold.

graph_edits.rationale: Retarget the dominant mass away from a sealed cantilever-block toward a split/void-oriented primary so the access edge can be read as a real public threshold.
Lower the overhang dominance to free more ground-level presence and reduce the boxy perched condition.
Bias the primary gesture toward a less monolithic cantilever vector so the public edge can be articulated.
Align the void to the verified access side so the street edge becomes a legible public opening rather than an internal subtraction.
Enlarge the court to produce a meaningful public room and make the void visible across views.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent stepped/cantilevered mass in all four views, so gesture clarity and repair integrity are decent. However, the ground response is weak: the blue access edge is not met by a clearly public, open, or carved threshold, and the visible void is mostly internal/insufficiently legible at ground. The silhouette is more an abstract stepped block than a convincing neighborhood-living mass with active street edge and public court logic. Programmatically, it can support mixed-use only in a generic sense; it lacks a strong public threshold and the section does not clearly reinforce the required street-building relation. The references support a courtyard/threshold strategy and a compact commercial urban host, while the tower reference is only marginally resonant and the bridge reference is counterfactual.
